# These tests pin the check that reports a delete the server lost, on both sides.
# Each false-negative test is green on the real server and red under one named server mutant: KEEPALL (a sibling
# edit after the deleting device leaves, a file added to the deleted folder, a folder rename the server kept),
# PATCHB (an unsent edit after the device leaves, an unseen rename of a folder above, the two carried-delete
# shapes), R8GROUP (a file added after the delete), and KEEPALL plus PATCHB (a rename to a folder between).
# Each false-positive test pins a legitimate revive that a rule version in this change or one ablated rule
# clause reports: another device's save, rename, move, folder rename or rollback, a conflict copy or copy,
# a restore its user chose, and a folder another device moves back under the server's last-writer-wins rule.
# The check judges another device's change by whether the deleting device's R held the commit that carried it,
# so a sim unit test pins which commits each device's R holds across acks, records, listings and a restore onto
# another branch whose new commits reuse its seqs, and that a resent change keeps the commit that first carried it.
# The ignored tests replay saved battery cases of the open engine bugs GUN-864, GUN-1054, GUN-1102 and GUN-1103.
# The devices properties can't stand in for them: they run this check only inside the property battery, where
# a missed delete is one case among thousands and a false positive turns the whole battery red.
